prs.title: fix(client): suppress onerror when SSE disconnect will be handled by reconnect
prs.author: felixweinberger
prs.cluster_pick_reason: CI is unknown for both and both touch 3 files, so the tiebreakers are approach and age. #1827 is the older PR (~April 2026 vs. #2124 from ~May 2026). On the technical approach: issue #1211 is an error-event race condition — when an SSE connection drops and a reconnect is already in flight, the onerror handler fires spuriously toward callers. #1827 fixes this directly on the client by suppressing that onerror event when a reconnect will handle the disconnect, a minimal, targeted change at the correct layer. #2124 addresses a contributing cause (the server letting idle GET SSE streams expire), but keeping streams alive is a different mechanism that does not eliminate the race condition itself; a stream can still drop for reasons other than server-side idle timeout. On equal CI and diff-size signals, #1827's earlier submission date and more direct correspondence to the reported symptom make it the stronger candidate to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: #2215 is a strict superset of #2214. Both apply the same `/\/+$/` regex fix to the two normalization sites, but #2215 also fixes a downstream correctness gap: after normalization a bare `/` pathname becomes `''`, yet `shouldAttemptFallback` was still checking `pathname === '/'`, so the root-path guard would never fire. #2215 patches that check to `pathname === ''` and extracts a shared `normalizeDiscoveryPath()` helper that keeps both call sites in sync, preventing the same drift from recurring. #2214 leaves those two issues unaddressed.
